'British West Florida was a colony of the Kingdom of Great Britain from 1763 until 1783'; created by the Royal Proclamation of 7 October 1763; the page says it comprised 'parts of the modern states of Louisiana, Mississippi, Alabama, and Florida' and gives the eastern boundary as the Apalachicola River in 1783; no area (the gazetteer's West Florida is 61,708 km2). The northern limit is the gazetteer's 31 N; the pages opened give none.

ledger.note: 1763: British West Florida is created. The Royal Proclamation of 7 October 1763 'created the province of Quebec, the colonies of West Florida and East Florida'; under the Treaty of Paris of 10 February 1763 'Spain ceded Florida to Britain' (West Florida page: in exchange for the return of Havana); capital Pensacola.

region.text: the Gulf coast of Alabama, Mississippi and Louisiana east of the Mississippi: Mobile and the Florida Parishes, ceded by France

ledger.note: 1763: the Gulf coast from the Mobile to the Mississippi, ceded by France in the treaty signed on 10 February 1763 and attached to West Florida by the proclamation of October 1763 (the month is the proclamation's). 'France also ceded the eastern half of French Louisiana, that is, the area from the Mississippi River to the Appalachian Mountains', and Article VII 'cedes in full right ... the river and port of the Mobile'. Which part of the eastern half became West Florida is the researcher's reading; the Treaty of Paris page does not name West Florida.

wars.name: Spanish conquest of British West Florida

zones.text: West Florida, the Gulf coast from Baton Rouge to Pensacola

wars.outcome: Gálvez took Fort Bute and Baton Rouge in September 1779, Mobile on 14 March 1780 and Pensacola on 10 May 1781; the Peace of Paris (1783) ceded West Florida and East Florida to Spain.
wars.note: No war article was opened; the Battle of Pensacola page describes the earlier captures. The page dates the siege 9 March to 10 May 1781 and gives no day for Fort Bute or Baton Rouge.

certainty.note: No survey on the pages: the northern limit (31 N, later extended according to other sources) and the eastern limit at the Apalachicola are approximate.

notes: Not a Cliopatria row (Cliopatria draws these years inside its British aggregates; the seed neighbours of spanish-florida show British Colonial Empire cells on the Gulf coast). Four pages: British West Florida, Battle of Pensacola (1781), Royal Proclamation of 1763, Treaty of Paris (1763). Not on the pages: the 1764 northward extension of the province, the 1783 dispute over the northern boundary with the United States (the spanish-florida dossier has it as a contest from 1783), Natchez, Fort Bute's day. The state ends at the 1781 conquest although the page dates the colony to 1783. The West Florida page: the eastern boundary was the Apalachicola in 1783; Spain moved it to the Suwannee in 1785. Counterpart: the spanish-florida ledger uses british-colonial-empire for the same events. Gazetteer: the 'West Florida' region is the 31 N coast and panhandle strip.
